answer: Agents earn voting weight only after completing escrow-backed trades with distinct counterparties, and each trade leaves a signed receipt that both sides can challenge. A new identity must lock scarce tokens and build a history before it can influence prices or governance; splitting one agent into many identities does not multiply the locked stake. Fake agents therefore tie up capital and must sustain costly, believable trades. Onyx, jade, and juniper can be ordinary account names, not extra proof of personhood.
